column1: # note: 29 directories in this slice, all 1995-c*. Every one had a blocks-by-ip.txt with real blocks and nonzero shares; no NORUN rows.
# note: GENUINE 3D / TEXTURE / INTERPOLATOR SHAPES (the demos that got the careful reading):

# note:   cass 1000:386 26.68% DOT3 -- 2x2 fixed-point rotation rows: movsx16 + imul by sin/cos constants (0x109d, 0xfe9) + sar#8, four rows unrolled, then a scale/perspective imul + sar#7 pair. The cleanest transform row in the slice.
# note:   cma_brw/BRW 8064d:453a 23.59% TEXEL_FETCH -- (u<<12) + (v<<6) + texbase, byte load, byte store, three spans unrolled at 0xa640 destination strides. Real texture addressing.
# note:   cma_brw/BRW 8064d:4604 10.02% FIXPT_STEP -- add [step_lo] / adc [step_hi] / stosb: a fixed-point accumulator whose carry advances the integer part, stored per pixel.

# note:   cma_brw/DOWNADD 1000:3c8 18.95% PERSP_DIV -- two cwd + idiv_r16 per point (x/z and y/z) with centre adds and clip compares; 1000:3ef (10.75%) then does the imul#0x140 addressing. A real 3D point projector.

# note:   countdwn/ZOKDTPLN 1000:673 68.51% BLEND -- 4-bytes-at-a-time SWAR average (a+b)>>2 & 0x3f3f3f3f; 1000:144 20.29% is the same effect byte-wise with neighbours at +0x13f/+0x27f; 1000:2c3 0.84% DOT3 is an imul + shrd#8 rotation pair.
# note:   cocobbs1/NM2 27c0:60 96.02% BLEND -- ((a<<2) + (b<<2) + c + d) over a scanline pair at +0x13f: a fire/blur kernel that is essentially the entire program.

# note:   ctslasse 0d:f2ab 18.77% and 0d:f1e6/f219/f241 24.03% BLEND -- 9-tap neighbour sum with add/adc 16-bit accumulation and a per-pixel idiv_r32 by the tap count. The divide is a blur denominator, not a projection, so it is tagged BLEND rather than PERSP_DIV.
# note:   cna_ply/POLLY 1100:415 42.75% CMP_SKIP -- lodsb / cmp 0 / conditional stosb: colour-keyed sprite blit.
# note:   cdz_frog/FROGFUZZ 1100:a83 9.07% FIXPT_MUL -- (a*b + 0x8000) >> 16 twice (u and v), a rounded 16.16 scale step.
# note:   crystal 1000:1c47 + 1c7f 68.58% FIXPT_STEP -- two accumulators stepped per iteration with an xor-into-memory plot. An XOR vector/DDA rather than a texture, but a genuine interpolator.
# note:   crap 7980:41 26.24% ADDR_SCALE -- (y<<8) + (y<<6) + x, the textbook shift-chain *320, guarded by two clip compares.
# note: CHROME 1000:106 (33.38%) is tagged OTHER: an in-place per-byte negate sweep (neg [mem]; inc; cmp). It is neither a fill nor a table lookup, so no ARITH tag fits; it is a one-op pixel map.
# note: confyooz/README! is a DOS int21 AH=02 character printer (98.84% in one three-block cycle) -- tagged OTHER, no arithmetic at all in the window.

# note: countdwn/COUNTDWN's entire top-40 is DPMI real<->protected mode switching and interrupt reflection (lgdt/lidt/cr0/iret/pusha32). Three CALL_GLUE loops, no arithmetic, and low shares (top block 5.04%) -- the window is spread thin across mode switches.

# note: creation/CREATION's hot blocks are all Turbo Pascal runtime glue reached by far calls (a 32-bit negate, a range check, a call/ret shell). Three loops, essentially no demo arithmetic in the window.
# note: cornetto/CORNETTO is 99.84% a two-block spin (cmp byte / loop) and has no third distinct loop worth a line.

# note: cenflash/CEN!FB (84.87%), clash (75.84%), coffee/COFFEE (35.08%), confyooz/CONFYOOZ (20.69%) and cornetto (99.84%) spend their windows in spin-waits. I tagged these IO_POLL even though they poll a MEMORY byte (an IRQ-set flag) rather than a port, because the semantics are the wait, not the arithmetic; clash's variant polls a status byte through a call/ret with two bit tests per iteration. Only cda_tp5i (in 0x60), crap (in 0x3da) and the out-driven PIT/DAC players (frog, ukko, polly, quartz, dope) are literal port I/O.

# note: the shl/dec/jz bit loop plus lodsb/rep_movsb at offsets 7f/86/8f/f3/f8 recurs byte-identically in catwalk, chrome, cma_stik/UKKO, cocaholc, coffee, cytopyge and clash -- it is ONE shared EXE-packer stub (bit-control-word LZ), not seven independent decompressors. That single stub inflates the REFILL and COPY_BACK counts across the whole slice.

# note: likewise the mul_m16 + add/adc/adc 3x3 partial-product block is byte-identical in cenflash 19250:3de1 and confyooz 6c10:e41 (one library routine: a 32/48-bit fixed multiply), and cocobbs1 COCONTS1/NM2 plus ctslasse 0d:f19c are LCG random generators (mul-add, high half taken). All four are tagged FIXPT_MUL, but none of them is a graphics interpolator.
